items.response:
Happy early birthday to Leo, eight already! Heads up that his skating lesson is Saturday 10:30 at Jimmie Simpson on 23 Jan, so I'd look for an afternoon slot, and since he's allergic to cashews and pistachios I'll also ask about their food and cake policy. I don't have Wonder Workshop's party details or prices yet, so I'll check rather than guess.
Action: Look up Wonder Workshop's party packages for 12 kids on Sat 2027-01-23 (afternoon slots, price, food/allergy rules) and report back.

Since the team already lives in Linear, Slack and Notion, I'd make one Notion database as the single inbox, with a #beta-feedback Slack channel as the easy way to dump things in. Starting columns: Merchant, Source (support email, sales call, update reply), Date received, Summary, Category (bug, UX, feature request, pricing), Severity, Status (New, Triaged, Ticketed, Won't do), Owner, and a link to the Linear ticket. Add a 'This week' view filtered to Status = New for the weekly triage.
Action: Create the Notion database and a draft of the Slack channel announcement, then share both with you to review before the team sees them.

On 2026-02-24 Tom had two openings: 10:00-10:30 and 15:30-16:00. The big May sync (2026-05-28) imported 14 events from Sam's school calendar.
Action: Nothing further needed unless you want me to pull the specific events from that sync.

Glad it landed. Aisha may now expect a poem a week.
Action: Nothing needed, ready when you are.

A dinosaur for Leo is the only acceptable choice. I'll look for a size 7 dinosaur costume under $50 that arrives before Fri 30 Jan, and I'll go with the best-reviewed one with a safe delivery date.
Action: Search size 7 dinosaur costumes under $50, order the best option that arrives in time, and send you the confirmation (I'll check with you first if shipping or tax pushes it over $50).

Since you and Priya both like mysteries, a Tana French hardcover would be a safe bet, but I don't know which of hers Priya has already read so I'll check stock and flag that. Draft card: 'Priya, a good mystery for a good weekend. So glad you're coming. Love, Riya.'
Action: Find a couple of in-stock hardcovers (Tana French or similar literary mysteries) with prices, and ask you whether Priya has read any of hers before I order.

Draft for #payouts-launch:
'Reminder: the beta retro is Thursday at 2pm in room 4B. Please add your sticky notes to the Miro board before then. Thanks all.'
Action: I'll post it in #payouts-launch once you say go.

For Marcus: 'Thanks, I'll think about it. I'm rethinking my whole routine at the moment.' For the card: 'Dear Grace and Daniel, thank you for having us for Christmas in Ottawa. We loved every minute of it, and the leftovers you sent us home with kept us going for days. With love and thanks from all three of us.'
Action: Send the reply to Marcus now, and once you OK the card wording I'll adjust the sign-off to your names.

Happy to find one. I'll look for upper-intermediate Spanish grammar books with a strong subjunctive section, plenty of exercises and a full answer key, and check which Spanish variety they use since I don't know your preference.
Action: Compare 2-3 candidates (price, reviews, answer key included) and send them to you before ordering.

Since Leo does best with one main activity and a quiet afternoon, I'd make the pumpkin patch the whole outing and be home for a calm late afternoon. I'll look for smaller farms within 45 minutes of home that are open today and not overrun, so you can leave around 1:30.
Action: Search pumpkin patches within 45 minutes, check today's hours and crowd reviews, and send a shortlist of 2-3.

Got it, short replies today.
Action: Keep everything brief and phone-friendly.

Obviously. Dinosaurs in the morning, pizza by lunch, a very efficient career plan. Sam's question and Leo's answer are a keeper.
Action: Want me to save this one to your notes with today's date?

One thing first: the cabinet delivery is Thu 16 Oct, 8:00-10:00, and someone needs to be home, but Thursdays are normally your office day, so you or Sam needs to cover it. Here's a start for the week: Mon unpack and laundry; Tue (office day) nothing big; Wed replace the furnace filter (16x25x1, due every three months, I'll check when it was last done) and check the upstairs bathroom door that sticks in humid weather; Thu be home for the cabinets; Fri pick a day for other pre-winter jobs.
Action: Put these in a Notes checklist and add a calendar hold for Thu 16 Oct 8:00-10:00 once you tell me who's home.

Fun, congrats to the team. I'll look for places near the King Street West office that can seat 8 on Thursday around lunchtime and have a proper vegan option for Wen, plus good vegetarian choices. I'll treat it as a lunch booking rather than my usual evening time, so tell me if you want a specific time.
Action: Shortlist 3 restaurants near the office with group seating for 8 and vegan options, and confirm the time with you before booking.

For Sam's birthday on March 22, he'd rather have a quiet dinner at home than a restaurant party, so a vegetarian (no fish) dinner you cook together fits, and gift-wise either the Fellow Ode coffee grinder he's wanted or a vintage Penguin paperback for his collection. One thing to sort out for the anniversary: I have two dates saved for it, June 8 and June 16, so which one do you want to plan around? Either way, you usually go out for dinner without Leo, so I can book early.
Action: Check Fellow Ode prices and vintage Penguin listings, and wait for your answer on the anniversary date before holding a table.

Draft for Olivia:
'Hi Olivia, good luck with Monday's call. I can't share a date for opening Instant Payouts beyond the beta merchants until Aisha has signed off, so for now I'd describe it as in beta with a limited group of merchants, and I'll send you a target as soon as it's confirmed. Happy to send the beta results so far for the call.
Best, Riya'
Action: Pull the current beta status and the latest on GA from Linear and Notion, check whether Aisha has signed off a target, and update the draft before you send.

Since it expires in January, I'd start soon. The usual checklist for a child's renewal: the application form, Leo's current passport, new passport photos, proof of citizenship if needed, ID and details for the parents or guardians, and the fee. I'll confirm the exact current requirements, fees and processing times on the official site rather than quote them from memory.
Action: Pull the official checklist and form for a child renewal, look up passport office appointments near us, and send you the earliest options.

I can't see the recurring debits until I go through the TD statements, and I don't have a record of an Amazon order for batteries, so I'll check your email and Amazon order status. From this conversation, I've set up: the data request draft for Wen, your weekly to-do roundup, the Saturday run on your calendar, the Bell Fibe internet check ($95 a month, unchanged), the payouts v2 PRD skeleton in Notion, and your Vancouver flight preferences. I can't list anything older than this chat.
Action: Pull monthly pre-authorized and subscription charges from the TD statements and look for the batteries order in your email, then report back.

Here's a short list for Priya. Pros: better retention and recruiting, less burnout, and people often protect their focus time more. Cons: client deadlines and coverage on the off day, possible longer days if hours stay the same, and billing or project timelines may need renegotiating. For an architecture firm, the big questions are client responsiveness and how deadlines get handled.
Action: Turn this into a polished message you can send to Priya, if you want it.

Sweet of you. I'll order an oat-milk flat white (nothing hazelnut) and a vegetarian snack with no fish, from a spot near Riverdale that delivers, timed for about 3:30 to room 214. I'll check whether the school office needs to receive deliveries.
Action: Find a nearby cafe that delivers, place the order for 3:30 to room 214, and send you the confirmation.

How about: 'Happy birthday, Tom. Thanks for being such a good person to work with. Hope it's a great day. Riya'
Action: Ready to paste into the card; tell me if you want it warmer or shorter.

Here's a 15-item checklist: windows and screens, wash curtains, declutter closets, clean behind and under big furniture, deep-clean the fridge and oven, wipe baseboards and doors, dust vents and light fixtures, flip or vacuum mattresses, clean the bathrooms top to bottom, organize the pantry, sort the garage and basement, clear the entry, swap seasonal clothes, wash the porch and entry mats, and restock cleaning supplies. For the couch, I'll look up the city's bulky item pickup and a couple of junk removal quotes, and I won't book without checking with you.
Action: Save the checklist to Notes and find options for hauling away the basement couch.

I don't have anything saved that says you bought or replaced them, so I can't tell you either way from memory. I'll check your email receipts, order history and calendar from before Christmas.
Action: Search for a furnace filter purchase or reminder and tell you what I find.

Sure. Leo has a tree nut allergy and the family keeps nuts out, so I'll keep everything nut-free (checking labels for 'may contain'), and I'll go with no-name brand basics where I can. I don't know whether Jun or his sister have any allergies, so is anything off the list?
Action: Build a PC Express cart of simple nut-free snacks for three kids, schedule pickup for tomorrow at 3:00, and send you the cart and total before checkout.

Partly. Written Portuguese is fairly readable for a Spanish speaker, so menus and signs should be fine, but spoken Portuguese is much harder to follow, especially European Portuguese in Lisbon, because the sounds are quite different. A few basic Portuguese phrases would go a long way, and many people in Lisbon will switch to English anyway.
Action: Add a short list of essential Portuguese phrases to your Lisbon note.

I haven't opened Carlos's email yet, so I can't judge it. Based on where you are, B1 heading to B2 with the DELE B2 in May 2026, extra conversation practice could be useful, but it would be on top of your Thursday 8:00 pm lesson and the current $180 for four lessons. I'll read it and weigh cost, schedule and fit.
Action: Read Carlos's email, compare it to your current lessons and calendar, and give you a worth-it or overkill verdict.

A few non-scented ideas: for Grace, a book of piano sheet music since she still teaches, and for Daniel, a book on bridges or engineering history given his civil engineering career. A nice local food gift like maple syrup, good tea or chocolate also works, and I'd steer clear of candles, soaps and anything perfumed. Tomorrow is Thanksgiving Monday, so I'll check which shops are open.
Action: Find 2-3 options in Ottawa open tomorrow with hours and prices and send them to you.

Added the action item: update the public roadmap page, owner you. That's a lot for one Saturday: Sandbanks, two wineries, the cheese shop, Lake on the Mountain and the lavender farm after an 8:00 departure will be tight with the drive and winery hours, so I'd suggest moving one or two stops (maybe Lake on the Mountain or the lavender farm) to Sunday. I'll check opening hours and whether Sandbanks needs a day-use reservation.
Action: Draft a Saturday and Sunday itinerary in driving order with times, and send it for your OK.

Sunday scaries are the worst, and an extra hour doesn't fix them. Nothing needs you tonight. One small thing that might help is picking a slot for the half hour with Aisha and Diego (Mon 3 Nov 13:30, Tue 4 Nov 14:00 or Wed 5 Nov 10:30) so it's off your mind.
Action: Send the invite as soon as you pick a slot; otherwise I'll leave you alone for the night.

Because of a poem from World War I: poppies grew on the battlefields in Flanders, and a Canadian doctor, John McCrae, wrote 'In Flanders Fields' about them, so the poppy became the symbol of remembering the soldiers who died. For Leo: 'Poppies were the first flowers to grow where soldiers were buried, so we wear one to say we remember them.'
Action: Nothing needed; I can find a short kids' video or book about it if Leo wants more.

Understood on the pet budget, we can look at it again whenever you and Sam are ready. I'll pull every open risk for the payouts launch from Linear into a single Notion doc for tomorrow's standup, with dates in ISO format since it's a work doc.
Action: Create 'Payouts launch risks (2025-11-12)' in Notion with owner, due date, status, mitigation and next step for each risk, and send you the link.

Draft to Hannah:
'Hi Hannah, you kindly offered to help with Biscuit a while back. Would you be able to feed and walk him while we're away from Thu 9 to Mon 13 July? We'll pay you, of course. He eats Purina Pro Plan Sensitive Skin & Stomach (salmon) because chicken-based food makes his skin itchy, so no chicken treats please. No worries at all if it doesn't work.'
Action: Send it to Hannah now.

For December, I don't know your plans yet, so I'll check your calendar for holidays, school breaks, trips and family commitments and propose which days to block as OOO or early leave. For 'that thing' last winter when school was shut, I don't have it saved, so I'll look through your calendar, notes and photos from around then.
Action: Draft a December OOO and early-leave list for you to confirm before Friday, and search last winter's records for what you did on the school closure day.

I'll reorder the dishwasher pods and paper towels, matching what you got last time. For the Dyson, I don't know which model Hannah has, so I'll find out and compare it with similar cordless options, but I'll check with you before buying since it's a bigger purchase.
Action: Reorder the pods and paper towels from your order history, and send you a short Dyson shortlist (with Hannah's model if I can find it) for your approval.

I don't have that search saved, so I can't tell you what we found. Times and fares will have changed anyway, so the best move is to run it fresh.
Action: Look up current VIA Rail Friday evening departures and fares from Toronto to Ottawa and compare them to the drive.

The closest match I have is the podcast episode about pricing for B2B APIs that you asked me to summarize, but I don't have its name or link saved. Let me find the summary so you send Aisha the right one.
Action: Search our history and notes for that episode summary, get the title and link, and draft a short note to Aisha for you.

I haven't opened the link yet so I don't have the price. When I do I'll show it in CAD with the rupee price in brackets, using 1 CAD = 63.4 INR (the 2025-11-01 rate I have, so it may have moved a bit). To judge whether it's reasonable, I'll compare similar silk sarees (weave, zari work and weight) on other sellers.
Action: Open the saved Kanchi Silks House link and report the price in CAD with INR in brackets, plus a comparison with similar listings.

That sounds perfect. Nothing needs you today, so I'll hold anything non-urgent.
Action: No pings from me unless something truly needs you.

That's a stressful feeling, and you're probably right that it's a dead phone, especially after a long weekend of travel. A good next step is a short, low-pressure text she can answer whenever she's charged, and try calling again at a time she's usually around. If you'd feel better, is there someone near her, like a family member or neighbour, who could quickly check in?
Action: Draft a short text to your mom and set a reminder to try calling again at a time you choose.

Good idea, Zoom should be easier for her. I'll find this week's call on your calendar (I'll ask if I can't see it), set up the Zoom meeting, and text her the link with a quick note on how to join.
Action: Create the Zoom meeting for the call time and text the link to your mom.

Will do, short replies until 5.
Action: Hold non-urgent items until after 5.

Happy long weekend! Here's a sensible order:
- [ ] Find the good extension cord
- [ ] Fix Leo's bike chain
- [ ] Hang the hallway mirror
- [ ] Sort the garage recycling
- [ ] Plant the tomato seedlings
Action: Save it as a checklist in your notes.

Birth date: Biscuit was born around April 2022, so write 'approx. April 2022' unless you have the exact date from his paperwork. Behavioural notes: very food-motivated and steals bread off the counter, and he howls at sirens. Medical-wise, chicken-based food gave him itchy skin and he now eats Purina Pro Plan Sensitive Skin & Stomach (salmon).
Action: Check his old vet records for the exact birth date, then fill in the intake form for you.

For a street-cleaning tow in Toronto, Hannah should first find out which tow yard has her car, using the city's towed-vehicle lookup or by calling 311 or parking enforcement. She'll need her ID, proof of ownership and insurance, and she'll pay the tow and storage fees plus the parking ticket. I'd rather check the current fees than quote a number from memory, and storage fees add up each day so she should go soon.
Action: Look up the current towing process and fees and send you a short summary to pass on to Hannah.

Approximately: flour 1 1/2 cups = 190 g, sugar 1 cup = 200 g, butter 1/2 cup = 113 g, plain yogurt 1/2 cup = 120 g, lemon juice 2 tbsp = 30 g, baking powder 1 tsp = 4 g.
Action: Want me to save the gram version to your recipes?
